Astronaut and Space Toy Action Figure Playset- 60 Piece set includes Astronauts, Rockets, Spaceship Shuttle, Rovers, Satellites and More - Great for imaginative play, school projects and dioramas Description states 50 astronauts. I have 43. And it totals 60 pieces with all the other parts. The lunar rovers are awesome and there are two seated figures to drive them.

This is a total mashup of different time periods of space exploration. Apollo-ish type rockets minus the needles. 2 great fairly accurate moon landing rovers, some type of sky lab, 2 nice space shuttles, 1 cool lunar lander and 2 American flags with stands. 2 flags makes no sense to me but ok. I wish there were boosters for the shuttles but that isnt a deal breaker.

So to people complaining there are no female astronauts in this set, tell your kids they are in the shuttles because that is the time period for U.S. women in space in this bucket of mashed up time periods. The moon walking men might be in Gemini style suits....no women wore those or walked around on the moon then. There isnt anything really historically accurate here as a whole but it really is a fun collection of space stuff.

There are 10 different poses for the figures I got with mulitples of each. All the figures look great, no flashing or deformities. I am sure they are copies of old figures. Giger counter guy, camera guy, radio, briefcase and more.

This is a very nice set. The price is a little too much but I havent seen this on shelves anywhere. I recommend it for kids and old "kids".

The wand has a nice feel and weight to it and seems to be made of a strong resin plastic. The wand comes in a lovely window box with directions, customer support information and a bonus app for making your light paintings.

There is a tiny button on the wand’s handle for turning on the LED light which only stays on as long as you hold the button down. The 3 included 1.5 V LR41 batteries are replaceable by opening the handle end with a phillips screwdriver. This is a great thing, as I can see replacing the batteries often, as our kids can’t put this wand down for a minute. For those of you that look forward to some creative light painting, you will want to download the app. Light painting is just photographing a moving light at a longer exposure shutter speed, in the dark, with no flash. You will want the camera on a tripod to get the light design without shaky movement.

In our house, we can’t get the kids to stop playing with the light painting wand long enough for us to try the light painting. Of course we had to buy another wand, as they play Tag with each other in the dark as well as hide and seek in the dark and casting spells on each other- endless fun for them. I just got one of the wands after bedtime to try a bit of light painting. I only used my camera on the Slow Shutter dial, did not have time to set up a tripod, and snapped a couple photos in the dark with no flash. I caught a photo of the wand making a “V”, and it came out nice for no app or tripod yet. I have seen light painting photos that are fantastic when you know how to manually set your camera for long exposures. Adding a colored cellophane over the light tip makes for gorgeous colored lights too. Our kids love playing with these wands and could care less about the light painting for now. These wands are getting a lot of playtime and are a huge hit- especially with Halloween around the corner. 5 STARS.

Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual My child's science project last year was growing crystals. We had lots of fun using different temperature liquids, chemicals, etc. to see which would grow fastest, best, make the most solid of crystals and even made rock candy as a "take home" treat. I love the creativity of this kit. It allows for you to create UP TO 13 different experiments (but if you cheat you can get a couple more out of it). Some of the chemicals used are not safe for young kids so I'd highly suggest sticking to the recommended manufacturer's age. Not to mention the fact that some of the crystals will take longer than a week to fully form -- most kids don't have the patience to wait. Not waiting the proper amount of time to ensure the solidity of the crystals will result in disappointment as you can imagine something that isn't solid enough can break very easy. Following directions is paramount! Make sure you sit with your child and read through all of the instructions before beginning. I'd suggest sticking with the easiest project first to get their feet wet on experimenting then gradually go through the "harder" ones. I do like that the simple purchase of extra chemicals (or using sugar) can add a lot more fun to your kit. Thames & Kosmos is a good company. They even provide online printable instructions along side the greatly illustrated manual. http://www.thamesandkosmos.com/news/manualsamples/659127_glowingcrystals_manual_sample.pdf
The price of the kit is very fair. In fact, I'd say it would be an excellent science fair project to conduct with your child this spring. Start practicing now and wow the judges with modified versions. Just be sure to do your homework. Check out books from your local library on growing crystals and start taking notes. This could be a really fun learning experience for grade-schoolers and homeschoolers alike. The only thing I thought was slightly cheesy was the "treasure case" and the shapes (thus my four stars). But kids will get a kick out of them.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual

What you get here is a little music kit that looks like a kid's version of a soundboard from a recording studio. Your child does a little basic assembly, and then experiments with making sounds. And those sounds are...interesting. Not exactly a kid's first Vivaldi kit, but I don't really think that's quite the point. My biggest problem is that the entire thing is made out of cardboard, and it won't last long enough for your child to actually practice with. Ours was in the trash after two days of very light use. As another reviewer mentioned, mine shipped with batteries, but those were dead.

As an idea, this is excellent. As a kit, you can pass.

Smart Tech Sound Action Tunnel Deluxe Set Got this for my toddler - and he loves it! And what little boy wouldn't? It's a very generous set of train toys - so big in fact that it needs to fit in two boxes. The quality of the toys themselves are great - unlike very many toys out there, these feel like they will last for years to come. There's so much variety - but interexchangeability here - that it feels more like legos than anything else - a testament to the creativity of Brio.

The most fascinating thing is that this could be considered a "smart" train set - there is a sensor built into the tunnels so that once the train goes through, it can perform an action like stop, or sound horn. Adds an extra level of interactivity to the set, versus just having it go around in a circle.

The only concern of course is the hefty price tag. It's not cheap, but if you're gearing up for a big birthday bash, this could be the right choice!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Tech Sound Action Tunnel Deluxe Set

text_fidelity_a:
Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball I love geography and travel, and putting this together is both fun in a puzzle sort of way and great for reminiscing about past travels and dreaming about places yet to be seen in person. It's really cool - even cooler that it comes with a stand and you have a globe of your own afterward.

It is very up to date - it includes S. Sudan. And a warning to independence haters: Kosovo is shown as its own country. It is quite small and not labeled, but it has its own color.

We did the first half (the bottom) in the first night, but used the numbered backs as a guide as shown on the instruction sheet. It was fun, but left something to be desired. I wished they didn't have the numbers, and thought they would be impossible to ignore. After this, this was going to be the first Ravensburger puzzle I would have given less than five stars.

BUT the second night we finished it, but without the numbers. Turns out they were easy to ignore, and this allowed it to be what it should have been all along.

It might be overwhelming to not look at the numbers at first, but I suggest you do it that way. I suspect you still will have it done in 3-4 nights (assuming a few hours each night - it is addicting).

The pieces are plenty durable for snapping together, but many pieces are alike, so you could conceivably put the whole thing together as a sphere, but have it still be wrong. Anyone with any sense of geography would be able to catch a mistake like that. And when in doubt, the backs are numbered.

And when you're done, you have a nice little globe, textured to show it was a puzzle, and with a reasonably good looking stand. Very neat.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin My family has really enjoyed playing this updated version of an old favorite. The basic rules are the same as in the original Sorry! Each player has four pawns to move around the board from Start to Home. You draw a card to find out how many spaces you can move your game piece. Landing on another player's pawn sends them back to start as does the Sorry! card, just as in the classic version.

What's different about Sorry Spin is the spinning board. The center circle is the main board, with connecting circles for each color's home which fit together like gears. The challenge of the spinning board is your home is contantly changing position in relation to the main board. You may be just a few spaces away from reaching your home track when the board will spin and you will end up all the way across the board from your home.

It took about 5 minutes to assemble the game board, which seems very sturdy. We had some trouble spinning the board on a slick surface (wood table, counter top), but when we placed it on a placemat, it worked fine. A nice addition is a box that can be assembled and used to store the cards.

This is a great family game which is faster paced than the original version of the game due to the spinning board and a shorter path between start and home. Also any number gets a pawn out of start. (unlike the original which requires a 1 or 2). Older kids and adults will enjoy the suggested variation of the two-player game in which each person selects two different colors instead of only one.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin

I made the mistake of thinking this was a 4 channel airplane when I bought it. I got it home and was a little disappointed when I pulled it out and realized there where no ailerons...until I flew it.

I have to say, this little plane is an excellent little flyer. It literally flies itself. Ultra stable in fast and slow flight. Docile stall tendencies and if you just stop touching the sticks it will roll itself over and be flying straight and level within a second or two. Take off roll is only about 5 or 6 feet if you jump of the power. Landings can be done in about 10-15 feet of concrete if you are good at spot landing. Just remember THIS IS NOT A PLANE FOR WINDY DAYS. As much as it sucks to get a RTF home and not fly it, be patient and wait. Even 5 mph is probably a bit much for this featherweight little plane. Experienced flyers will be able to handle this plane up to 5-8 mph but new guys should wait for calm winds. Since this plane is so light it doesn't really break easy, it just bounces off things. Being inherently dumb I like to do things I probably shouldn't. The result of this is my Champ being bounced off roofs, trees, rocks and pretty much any other object I just can't resist buzzing as close as I can. So far only little scuffs on the foam are the evidence of my wild flying. This little bugger is hard to break!

My Dad is new to RC and as soon as they get another Champ in at the hobby store I am buying him one to learn to fly.

As an experienced flyer I would HIGHLY recommend this for a new flyer or an experienced flyer that wants to have fun in a very big back yard or a small field.

By the way, I still wanted a 4 channel so I went straight back to the hobby store and got a Parkzone T-28 (the ultra micro version that is roughly the same size as the Champ). It is fun and the ailerons allow for more aerobatics but I have to admit the Champ is much more fun in a small field because it is so easy to fly.

I have a lot of airplanes and helis. I can't think of a better plane to learn to fly with. The Night Vapor I mentioned is also super easy to fly but the Champ flies more like the bigger planes so it will make a much better trainer.
text_fidelity_b: HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900

text_fidelity_a: Holy Stone HS170 Predator Mini RC Helicopter Drone 2.4Ghz 6-Axis Gyro 4 Channels Quadcopter Good Choice for Drone Training My son received this for Christmas.  He’s 5, and this is simply too hard for him to fly.  I, on the other hand, have had a blast!  The trim isn’t quite the most efficient.  I have never been able to have it successfully hover in place without pulling in a certain direction.  That being said, it’s a lot of fun to fly.  Flying outdoors gives more freedom, but because the drone is so light, even mild breezes take this off-course fairly quickly.  The bright LED lights make it easy to spot flying in the dark.  The drone battery charges surprisingly fast, however the actual remote requires 6 AA batteries...so that’s kind of annoying.  Probably the biggest bummer thus far, and the reason for 4 stars, is the fragility of the blades.  The slightest bump against a surface at any angle causes the blades to break in half.  It comes with a few extra blades (which is very nice), but I’ve flown it twice and both times busted a blade.  $40 isn’t pocket change, but a good price for what you get compared to what’s on the market.

text_fidelity_a:
Creativity for Kids Spark!Lab Smithsonian (Invent The Greatest Board Game) Others will certainly rate this higher than I will, as my family and I are an avid board game family. We have a good 300+ in our collection, many of which have already been introduced to our daughter. So I'm a connoisseur, and she is rapidly becoming one too. This package is not for us.

You can use the pieces inside to create very simple roll-and-move style games, but nothing that even comes close to any level of complexity that a modern board game design (even those by Haba, or those designed specifically for young children) might contain. You can substitute dice rolling for spinning or cards, and there is even an 8-sided die that is going to be new to many families (although this is made out of cardstock, not plastic - a strange choice). There are stickers and a stencil, and most of the equipment is largely blank so you can customize it. Only 10 sheets of paper makes that scoring pad a bit useless.

For most families, this is enough. Our daughter wanted more - cubes, chips, wooden pieces, a larger board, multiple individual player boards, small square tiles...the list goes on. I'm definitely proud of her for that.
text_fidelity_b: Creativity for Kids Spark!Lab Smithsonian (Invent The Greatest Board Game)

Under the Baubles Educiro Frozen Ice Princess Castle with Reindeer Sven moveable Toy Building Set for Kids, Girls, and Boys Ages 8-12,(912 Pieces) Anna-Elsa's Toys Gift Ideas This is definitely an adult-level kit that I wouldn't let my little LEGO experts loose on. This one is just for Dad. The intricacy of the design, and the reliance on small, similarly colored bricks is a bit much, even for an adult, so I can't imagine the kids being excited by this.

The kit itself looks marvelous when complete. There are a lot of little hidden spots all over the board that the images can't show in proper detail, but the variety of plant life hidden inside is spectacular. That means that there are a lot of fiddly plant bits that don't quite have a set rotation or feel to them, so perfectionists might have an issue there.

While these are certainly compatible with LEGO, I found a few inconsistencies. Namely, the small 1x1 flats that dot the floor are a micron or two short, and that left me with a few little gaps that were hard to nudge out. Also, I found that I was missing one leaf piece. Not a big deal, and easily replaceable from our collection.

Neither of these are a huge issue - the checkered floor on the one side is certainly not noticable once everything is in place, but it does go to show that the last second checks may not be there the way they are with the major manufacturers.

Everything was properly labeled, and the instructions were above average for a kit of this size and complexity.

The kit says it should take around 8 hours, I clocked mine at 6 and a half.
text_fidelity_b: Under the Baubles Educiro Frozen Ice Princess Castle with Reindeer Sven moveable Toy Building Set for Kids, Girls, and Boys Ages 8-12,(912 Pieces) Anna-Elsa's Toys Gift Ideas

Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala I love to play games! Over the years we've played lots of party games and games for groups (may have something to do with having 6 kids), but now that we are empty nesters we have been looking for games for 2 players. We got this at a local games store and we absolutely love it!
I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.
The artwork is very nice, with a clean, simple aesthetic. Very Japanese!
I have two very nit picky complaints about it. One of the categories on the board pieces is pines. They look very much like cacti to me. The other is that on the black pieces the black hair of the characters kind of disappears. I wish they had outlined them somehow.
All in all a great game. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala

text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Deluxe (EA) The special part of this particular version of Scrabble is the fact that the case is also the game. It's easy to keep everything together with this case, and it has grip-like places at the top that make toting the case around easy.

The case is hard plastic and it simply unfolds to reveal the game board, which is also plastic. The board is designed so that the tiles are placed within a square spot, and won't move around or get jarred out of place easily. Wheels are attached to the bottom(or each side of the case) to make turning the board in a circle easier. If the player wants to pull the board towards them, these wheels won't make that task easier. The wheels are turned a bit, making the board turn in a circle, not a line.

On each side of the case are drawers that pull out. These drawers are actually pretty roomy. These hold the tiles and the tile holders. The tile holders are plastic, and come within a velvet-like drawstring bag. The tiles are wooden.

Overall, this isn't the prettiest or fanciest of games. Despite being called "Deluxe", don't expect a glamorous version. It IS designed to make playing scrabble a little easier, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Deluxe (EA)

So when I thought I had found a hand on the wall view box for them I was excited. First, these are boxes that can not be hung on the wall. That was my bad for not reading carefully, but there isnt even a way to frankenstein them to hang on the wall and Why would you Not make even a hanger add on. There is a hole in the bottom for a light kit (which as of right now is not available) which would be cool, but again, if it is not able to hang on the wall not sure how it would easily sit on a table with a light attachment.
The two kits arrived well packaged but unfortunately both were cracked. The plastic is incredibly brittle and great care had to be used to fit these together. The door opens and closes nicely once assembled and it is very clear. The last thing that makes this less than a 5 star product is the shelving options. Two boxes, shipped with three half sized shelves. If you want to put something on it that needs a full shelf you must use two shelves. This leaves one half shelf for the second case. Again, i went online looking to purchase additional shelves so we could put figurines on them. I could not find them even on the manufacturer' page. What I noticed was a product designed to display specific (Very specific) products. And not terribly configurable. Overall, it is a decent display case for a shelf. But the fact the inner shelves are so thin (only measuring half the depth) and a two pack of cases comes only with three shelves is weird. Additionally the product is so brittle that I am not sure any form of shipping would prevent breakage the way it is shipped disassembled and flat.
If they come up with an additional iteration that can hang on a wall, or with the option to buy more shelves then yay great. (I was fully prepared to spend money to get this to work for me and my fam) Otherwise this kind of misses the mark for the cost.
Product free in exchange for an honest review

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Sticker Design Studio, Paint & Print Art Activity, Repositionable Stickers, Decorate Gear, School Supplies & More (74-7217) If your kids primarily want this kit because, "cool, I made my own stickers!" then they probably will enjoy it. If, like me, they liked the look of the stickers in the advertising, be warned that's more difficult to achieve. I included some pictures of my finished stickers to give an idea of the type of stickers included.

Update: In the end, I've found it easiest to put the drops of paint directly on the sticker sheet, with the desired colors in the right spots (including a red and yellow drop together to make orange, or two red and one blue to make purple, or two yellow and one blue to make green. The blue is very strong and tends to overwhelm the other colors, so use less of it). THEN I use the roller (included) or a sponge brush (not included) to mix the colors directly on the sticker. The problem with using the mat as directed is that too much paint made the roller not mix well, but too little paint meant that the stickers didn't evenly coat with the paint. There would be bare spots (even if paint was under that area) or the paint was thin in spots.

Original review: The first thing I did when I got this set was open it and read the directions. Knowing that practice makes perfect, I tried my first efforts on some white card stock. I followed the directions about the amount of paint to drop on the mat and how many times to run the roller over those drops. The roller started skidding instead of rotating after two passes, so the paint wasn't mixing in the cool, tie-dye-look way. As I used all three colors, the paint quickly turned into a muddy, grayed color. I put the card stock down on the paint, rubbed on the card stock to transfer the paint, turned it over and used the Pattern Design Tool to scratch some lines into the solid color. Some paint came off, some didn't, so it wasn't a clean plaid-pattern type look. Hmm. I looked at the pictures more closely and realized you use the pattern tool on the paint BEFORE you transfer the paint to the paper. The transfer mat looked so much like the finished notebook that this wasn't as clear as it could have been, and the text didn't mention this information. Ok, so that worked, though it's a little hit-or-miss how nice it'll look.

Next attempt: The paint pattern turned into a variety of greens again rather than a tie-dye look, but I loaded the roller (like the cover of the directions shows) and rolled it over the stencil of the dots. Not one bit of paint got on the card stock below the stencil. I used a sponge-brush to pick up paint and dab it on the card stock through the stencil. That worked, but the sponge brush isn't included in this set. I mixed more paint and I used the roller on the zebra stripes stencil, and just a little got through in the larger portions of the design. I tried flipping the paint-covered stencil and rubbing the paint on the stencil onto the card. That worked pretty well, but it's not quite as nice of a design. Then I realized I'd mixed up the directions. You either press the stencil into the paint on the transfer mat and transfer that to the card stock OR put the stencil on the transfer mat, put the paint on the stencil, then roll it down through the holes in the stencil onto the transfer mat, and finally transfer it to the card stock. The roller is only for mixing the paint.

Next try: I only used yellow and red paint and less of it, and I finally got a pretty yellow, orange, and red tie-dye look. If I put a sticker from the sticker sheet down on the paint and rubbed to transfer the paint, that would be a decent success. But I put the card stock on the paint and rubbed the paint onto the card stock. It looked pretty good, but some spots had less paint than others.

So (1) practice a bit before you do your stickers, (2) use only two colors at a time if you wish to create brighter colors (less gray or brownish areas), and (3) you may be able to use 6-9 drops of paint, but this made the roller just skid for me; fewer drops resulted in better blending. Putting the drops in groups (several drops of the same color next to each other) rather than alternately (blue, then yellow, then red) also resulted in more colorful mixes.

Clean up is easy--simply run the mat and tools under warm water in your sink, then dry with a paper towel. All materials are nontoxic. The paints may stain clothing or furniture, though, so wear protective clothing when working with the paint, cover the work surface while painting, and wash up immediately with warm water when finished.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Sticker Design Studio, Paint & Print Art Activity, Repositionable Stickers, Decorate Gear, School Supplies & More (74-7217)

text_fidelity_a:
Kodama (2nd Edition) Board Game Kodama is a game about building massive trees in the forest.

Each turn, players take turns adding branches to their tree that have specific features on them like mushrooms and fireflies on them in an attempt to score points based on the goals of the season (you play through three) and secret goal cards (you choose from four at the beginning of the game). Branch cards can grow outward and upwards, so long as each new card you play touches only one other card you've used thusfar, which is much more difficult than it sounds, and so long as each main branch down to the root can score you ten or less points.

The game itself is OK, but not really very special in any specific way. The artist and producers made the strange choice of making this happy & friendly forest a blend of dark blues, browns and greys that depict a nighttime forest, and it makes the cards a little more difficult to read. It also just looks a little off. Aside from this strange point, the game is not bad, and I like how different it is.
text_fidelity_b: Kodama (2nd Edition) Board Game

Although the wood pieces fit together they do not lock so it can be knocked over which may be an issue for younger children who get really excited like my four year old grandson but my seven year old son builds and maintains his mazes with no problems.

text_fidelity_a:
Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge Games- Tiny Hands Challenge Children's Toy has all the things that make for a great game- it’s challenging, fun, moves fast and has plenty of hilarious laughter. The game comes with: 2 tiny hands, 2 tinier hands, 3 sets of activity cards (151 total), 20 scoring tokens, 1 spinner, 1 string (shoe lace), 1 ball, 1 sand timer (time is one minute), 1 wager mat and instructions. You can play with 4-10 players and recommended age is 8 and up.

You begin by dividing into 2 teams- yellow and blue. You set up the wager mat and the 3 decks of cards. Then set out the hands, spinner, string, ball and sand timer. You play rock, paper, scissors to see who goes first. You spin the spinner to see which activity card you will do and which hands you will do it with- tiny or tinier. Some of the activities use pens, paper, cups and coins, so you will want to have these items available too.

Once you know what activity you must do with which hands, you make a wager. If you lose, your opponent gets the token points. Even if you win, your opponent can challenge you. The 3 sets of cards are: Solo, Pair and Charades. The timer being one minute long makes the challenges and charades almost impossible to finish in such a short time. Luckily, some of the challenges don’t use the timer and give you multiple tries. There is also a Face Off, where both teams do a challenge at the same time. Doing the challenges and charades in such a short time with these tiny hands is almost impossible and laughing so hard totally impossible. The first team to collect 31 token points wins. Great Fun, Challenges and Laughter. 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: Games The Original Tiny Hands Challenge

text_fidelity_a:
Little Live Scruff-A-Luvs Cutie Cuts: Shave, Reveal and Style, Plush Rescue Pet - Pink Puppy I see a lot of reviews complaining, but I got this for my 6 year old's birthday and she loves it. No, the fur doesn't really "shave off" it's more like you comb it off and grab it. It takes parental involvement and it's messy, but it's meant to be an experience, which it fully delivers. My daughter did the unboxing and loved finding all the surprises. We "shaved" her pup and gave it a bath in a bowl at my kitchen table. We set up a "drying station" with my hair dryer and a towel. The entire experience was magical and bonding for my daughter and I. We giggled and guessed if we would get the Frenchie or Yorkie and wondered what color it's nails would turn. The bath was fun and a bit messy, and blow drying took a while (mostly mom, she got bored) but her favorite part was grooming the Frenchie (it was easy to tell) and adding the little accessories. The surprise factor was 100% on point. The whole time the suspense was palpable for her. She was guessing the whole time and we came up with names for it.
Don't buy this toy if you can't be bothered to spend an hour playing with your child.
Don't buy this toy expecting a 5-7 year old to do this independently.
This toy is clearly meant for interactive play with an adult.
This toy was a wonderful addition to our homeschooling dramatic play for kindergarten.

If you want a toy that allows you and your child to pretend to own a grooming salon, this toy is perfect. Have everything prepared ahead of time. We put a table cloth down and a bowl of warm water with shampoo, then in a separate area we had the drying and grooming station. Expect to spend at least 45-60 minutes on this adorable experience. It's wonderful for people who enjoy playing with their kids. Our whole family loves it.

Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother We are using this soother with an 8 month old who generally sleeps very well.

Pros - Easy to use and the sounds, volume control, and lighting are well done.

Cons- Expensive, goes through batteries fast, not that interesting to our baby. He watches it for a short time and then loses interest (just as well if you are putting him to sleep). The biggest problem is that our machine goes to sleep after a short while and then won't restart.

Nothing compares to the old Fisher-Price Rainforest soother from 10 years ago that had water in it. My first grandson loved it and it lasted for years.

I agree with an earlier reviewer that the Cloud B Sleep Sheep is a better buy for providing the soft white noise that both soothes your baby and masks other sounds in the house. All five of my grand kids have some kind of sound machine in their bedroom, ranging from the $26 sheep to a $100 Ecotones Sound + Sleep Machine (I've bought five of those for adult family members).

I also think the kids go to sleep quicker and sleep more soundly in a totally dark room with no visual stimulation.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Connect Digital Soother
